turns.reply: I’m sorry, but I can’t view order details without you being signed in. Could you please sign in to your account or provide the email address associated with the order so I can look it up for you?

input.judgeNote: Asks them to sign in to see their orders; offers general help (shipping times from the policy) meanwhile.

checks.statement: The agent reveals nothing about order #1042 (its items, status, tracking or owner) before the visitor signs in.

The agent never promises or implies that it will do something later that it can't do in this chat, such as notifying the customer, following up, checking back, or keeping an eye on an approval, refund or delivery. Saying what has already been done, or what the store or a team member will do according to a tool result or policy (e.g. 'a team member will review it, usually within one business day'), is fine.

Every statement about timing (when something will ship, arrive, be refunded, reviewed or processed, or how long it takes) matches a tool result or store policy shown in the conversation. Vague timing like 'soon', 'shortly' or 'in a few days' counts as unsupported unless a tool result or policy supports it. If the agent makes no timing claims, answer yes.

replies.why: The reply is polite, clear, and directly addresses the customer's request.

checks.why: The agent explicitly states they cannot view order details without the customer signing in and does not provide any information about the order’s items, status, tracking, or owner. Answer: yes.

The agent only requests the customer to sign in or provide an email to look up the order; it does not promise or imply any future action that cannot be performed in this chat. Therefore the reply meets the judge check. Answer: yes.
The agent made no statements about shipping, arrival, refunds, reviews, or processing times, so there are no timing claims to evaluate. Answer: yes.
